answer: Agents can make costly actions—placing work offers, voting, or claiming rewards—require a refundable bond locked for a fixed period, with a small portion forfeited when independent audits catch coordinated duplicate identities. Audits compare behavior and shared control signals, not merely names, so an attacker cannot cheaply multiply influence by minting accounts. The bond ties each attempted sybil to capital at risk; echo, yarrow, and voyage can be harmless account names, but each still needs its own locked stake.
